speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You presented with delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history of bone fragility; to begin our evaluation, have you experienced any fractures after minor trauma or fallen from a standing height?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: 17-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency.

The combination of ambiguous genitalia at birth (clitoromegaly), lack of pubic hair (implied by the mother's chin hair and your delayed menarche), and a family history of hypertension suggests a defect in mineralocorticoid synthesis leading to undervirilization and hypogonadism.

REQUEST TEST: Plasma electrolytes, 17-hydroxyprogesterone, 11-deoxycorticosterone, and 11-deoxycortisol.
